sections.title: Two Names, Two Jobs
sections.body: Every device carries BOTH addresses. The MAC identifies the physical network card; the IP identifies where the device lives in network logic.
sections.code:
MAC: a4:5e:60:1f:22:9b   (48-bit, burned into NIC)
IP : 192.168.1.50        (32-bit, from DHCP or manual)

sections.title: Post Office Analogy
sections.body: IP is like a postal ADDRESS on an envelope (changes when you move house). MAC is like the persons NAME inside (stays forever). ARP finds which MAC owns which IP on your LAN.

sections.title: Working Together
sections.code:
PC-A -> PC-B same LAN:
[dst MAC B | src MAC A][dst IP B | src IP A]
Switch reads the MAC layer.
Router reads the IP layer and
rewrites MACs at every hop.

sections.title: Exam One-Liner
sections.body: MAC = who you physically are on this cable. IP = where you logically live in the world.
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: MAC stays constant across networks; IP changes as the device moves.
